summary: A notice that the Network Working Group meeting at MIT's Project MAC moved ahead two weeks, to October 10 through 14, 1971. It also sets the theme: with implementation largely done, the group's concern was shifting from protocols toward how the network is actually used.

plainLanguage.summary: This notice changes the dates of a Network Working Group meeting and explains its program. The group planned to focus on how people could use the network because much of the implementation work was complete.

sections.title: New Dates and Meeting Theme
sections.content:
MIT's Project MAC agreed to host the next Network Working Group meeting in Cambridge, Massachusetts. Scheduling conflicts moved the dates in RFC 207 ahead by two weeks. The meeting was scheduled to begin on Sunday, October 10 at noon and end on Thursday, October 14.

The group had mostly worked on communications and protocol implementation. Since implementation was substantially complete, the notice identifies network use as the meeting's main theme.
sections.plainLanguage: The meeting dates changed because of scheduling conflicts. The group also planned to focus on ways to use the network, now that much of the implementation work was complete.

sections.title: Meeting Phases and Sessions
sections.content:
The meeting has three phases. A system programmers workshop runs from Sunday noon through Monday. The second phase begins Tuesday morning and includes a review of standard protocols, a tutorial on using the Network Information Center (NIC), and a session about Terminal Interface Message Processors (TIPs).

The third phase starts Wednesday with reports on the workshop, protocol review, network services and developments at several sites. On Thursday morning, representatives of service centers and user groups discuss access to those centers over the network.
sections.plainLanguage: The program starts with a workshop, then offers a protocol review, a NIC tutorial and a session about TIPs. Later sessions report on network developments and discuss access to services.

sections.title: Participation and Arrangements
sections.content:
The protocol review is jointly chaired by John Postel of UCLA and Alex McKenzie of BBN. The NIC tutorial is limited by the number of available consoles, and the TIP session is open to interested participants. The Thursday round-table discussion is open to the public and invites audience participation.

Attendees are asked to register with Anne Speare. The notice says that hotel rooms have been reserved and will be assigned in the order requests arrive. It promises a later schedule listing workshop times and rooms.
sections.plainLanguage: Some sessions have limited places, while others are open to interested people or the public. Attendees must register, and hotel rooms are assigned in the order people request them.
